_doc: RFC 156 — the checked-in record of which GitHub Actions workflows a release (a push to main) is required to trigger. scripts/release-gate-manifest-check.sh compares this against what GitHub actually triggered for a commit; a mismatch means a gate silently stopped running, or a new workflow was added without being recorded here. See docs/src/expert/contributing.md#ci-gate-parity.

not_on_release_path.reason: Triggers on pull_request (path-filtered to crates/core/src/jwt/** and fuzz/**), a weekly schedule, and workflow_dispatch — never on push, so no release commit is covered by it. RFC 156 §4.1: a fuzz run is non-deterministic, and a release gate that can fail for reasons unrelated to the change under release is a bad release gate. The JWT parser (RFC 005) is independently-implemented code processing adversarial tokens on every request, so coverage still matters — the PR path filter plus the weekly schedule provide it without putting a non-deterministic job on the release path.
